All locales (languages) activated in JA must be aligned with languages currently supported/activated in JI

Alignment of time zones, countries and languages in JI. For example, in JA there are only 80 or so time zones which can be selected, while JI offers many more which are not compatible with the supplier sync. Languages in JA not supported in JI can remain for suppliers that need those languages in JA but these are not supported for internal users.

JI Business Unit with JA Buyer Account (BU internal name stored in Buyer Account External Unique Code field) if the multi-Business Unit license is active. Otherwise a unique reference (e.g. customer’s name) should be inserted in the JA Buyer Account “External Unique Code” field via the Support Console by editing the “Buyer Organization Profile” (utilize the JI.businessUnit parameter to specify the target JA Buyer Organization when requesting activation).

Alignment of the JA Buyer Organization “Division Names” with the JI Business Unit “Department Internal Names”. If implementing many JI Departments to one JA Division, utilize the JI.divisionName parameter to specify the target JA division when requesting activation. NOTE: the JA default “Division” should be renamed before aligning with the JI Department names.
Alignment the JA User Roles with JI user “Positions” (renamed in JI to “Sourcing Role”).

Configuration of the Business Unit (if applicable), Department and Position fields to be mandatory in the JI User Profile (renaming the Department field to "Division" and Position field name to “Sourcing Role”), since these are required to create the user in JA

Migration of all current JA users (both super and sub-users) to JI, ensuring that they are created with the same username and corresponding Business Unit, Department and Position (JI supports mass upload via Excel).

Deactivation of the JI system setting “Allow case-sensitive user names” within the Site Profile Miscellaneous Settings area (since JA does not support case sensitive usernames and will not be recognized by the SSO)
Activation of the default Authentication method to “JAAuthLogin” in Site Profile > Site Profile Integration Settings > General tab > Integration General Attributes (“Default Auth Source”)
Set the JI user profile setting “Authentication Method” is set to “JAAuthLogin" to allow SSO from JA to JI. Once set, users cannot login to JI directly.

Set in JI: Session Timeout URL URL to which the JAGGAER Indirect solution is to redirect users if their sessions time out Inactivity Timeout Time, in seconds, that the session will remain active if there is no activity by the user. Maximum Session Lifetime Time, in seconds, that the session will remain active after a user logs in, even if there is activity by the user. Set to 0 for no timeout.
In JI, provide user roles with permission to Sourcing -> Access Sourcing+ so that users can SSO back to JA.
All of the JA supplier registration fields must be used for their intended purpose (E.g. the address2 field in JA corresponds with the first address line in the default Remit To address in JI)
Activation of all JA additional address supplier registration fields (administrative address fields) which are used for the “Remit To” address for Invoicing

Activation of the “External Code” and “External Unique Code” profile field for suppliers/buyers, configured to be hidden in supplier registration and supplier portal view and editable on buyer organization profile. Populate JI Business Unit with JA Buyer Account (BU internal name stored in Buyer Account External Unique Code field) if the multi-Business Unit license is active. Otherwise the customer’s name should be inserted in the JA Buyer Account “External Unique Code” field.
Creation of a specific JA Supplier Extended Profile form which will hold a specific set of JI related supplier parameters and fields (see supplier integration section for specific field info)
Align the “Secondary Status” in JA with the “Supplier Classes” in JI, would need to have the same external code (internal name).
Create the JI Supplier class with the internal name “JASupplier” to indicate where the supplier was created (the class name can be defined as necessary, although we recommend “JA Supplier”)

If the supplier synchronization with JI was active in JA before the 19.1 release, all of the JA suppliers must be manually resync-ed with JI to ensure that the new JA Supplier ID field has been defined JI side. This can be done by downloading all of the JI enabled suppliers and modifying them massively (e.g. changing any field value before doing a bulk supplier update/upload).
Load JI Suppliers into JA if needed. Obtain the JA Supplier Account ID for each supplier.

Within Setup -> Site Profile -> Site Profile Integration Settings, set "Master Supplier Management" dropdown to SVM. This would allow the additional Supplier Management section of the Administration part of the User Permissions to be enabled. Update appropriate roles with the Supplier Management rights (Supplier Directory Access, Create New Supplier).
Within Field Management, search for "Add Suppliers". Set this field to be not visible so that users cannot create suppliers directly in JI.
Deactivate JA parameter SESSION_CSRF_CHECK. Otherwise there will be a cross site forgery error when using the new Supplier Management menu.
Activation of JA parameter GP_BLOCK_USERS_EDITING = F;null which will stop the end-users from modifying their user profile in JA, since JI will become the master system for user data
Activation of JA parameter GP_BLOCK_USERS_CREATION = 1;0 to turn off the “Create User” option in JA User Management, preventing all users from creating new users in JA (as they must be created in JI)

Configure the content of the JI login page so it is extremely clear that the user must use JA for logging in as the JI login page will not work for any user (e.g. https://solutions.sciquest.com/apps/Router/Login?OrgName=BravoDemo)

Alignment of JA category and JI commodity codes, ensuring that there is an equivalent JI commodity code for every selectable JA category tree node code (this is only required in the supplier category or RFQ/Auction object category selection parameters are activated).
Activation of the JA parameter STRUCTURED_FIELD to enable the admin defined UOM and Currency codes
Alignment of JA UOMs with corresponding codes and descriptions used in JI
Alignment of JA Currencies with corresponding codes and descriptions used in JI
Activation of Contract Manager Repository license within JI to ensure that the Contract Import API will be enabled (only applicable for RFQ/Auction to JI Contract integration)

Finally, when the integration parameter JI_TCM has been activated, you must manually enable the JI Contract module “service” in the Buyer Organization through the MOC Support Console area (clicking into the buyer organization profile and enabling the JI Contracts attribute).

Import Object level Category codes (xxxx.JI.contract.enableCommodity): Categories are imported into the contract as commodities, which must be mapped to the commodities in JI. Parameter value: blank or "0" = not mapped, 1 = mapped
Active JA RFx > JI Contract Integration
Activation of the JA parameter GOODS_GROUP, configured as visible and optional in the RFQ object (only required in the PR-RFQ-PR integrations)
Alignment of commodity codes in JI with Goods Group codes in JA, ensuring that there is an equivalent Goods Group code for every JI commodity code (only required in the PR-RFQ-PR integrations)
Creation of JA Additional Information fields and RFQ Form and Type which will hold additional data coming from the JI PR (see section on PR to RFQ integration for specific field info)

The Document Export “General Export Configuration” settings must be set to allow the Export of all PR custom field values, using the latest version of the PR export DTD (version 3.0). The “History XML Export Flag” can be activated or deactivated without any impact on this flow.

In order for the “Initiate Sourcing RFQ” button to become available, the workflow step configuration must include the flag “AllowCreateSourcingEvent as shown below: <Activity name=""Needs Sourcing?""> <ActivityType>manual</ActivityType> <StepRef name=""Needs Sourcing?"" /> <FolderRef name=""Needs Sourcing"" /> <Rule><![CDATA[Document.HasLinesNeedingSourcing in {""true""}]]></Rule> <FolderSelectionRule>ExplicitFolder</FolderSelectionRule> <Flag>NoBypass</Flag> <Flag>AllowCreateSourcingEvent</Flag> <Attribute name=""wfReturnReqInsteadOfReject""> <AttrValue lang=""default"">True</AttrValue> </Attribute

The creation of some JA Additional Information questions must be completed before the integration can be activated, which will allow some specific PR data to be stored in the RFQ to facilitate the reconciliation of data when the final PR is generated from the awarded RFQ. Fields to be created (see integration guide for more information). The customer can decide which fields they prefer to add to the RFQ additional information form in order to make the fields visible in the RFQ UI, without any impact to the integration flow. • PREPAREDBY_USERNAME • REQUISITIONER_USERNAME • REQUISITION_ID • REQUISITION_EXTERNAL_ID (optional) • REQUISITION_BU (optional)
Activate JI PR -> JA RFx and JA RFx -> JI PR integrations.
If only have TCM module in JI, ensure that user has "Contract Manager" right otherwise user cannot access JI from JA. This right is needed to access the Contract dashboard.
After integrations have been activated, review newly activated user permissions in JA and update appropriately.

In the case of the JA Contracts to JI Contracts flow, the TCM license in JI must not be enabled (only CCT and Contract Repository), the JI Contract type “Procurement” (Internal Name = “Procurement”) must be created as the only contract type, and all options to manually create JI Contracts disabled (via permissions and hiding main menu options via field name management)
